new.n: Camden Park bank-loot roll ($9,000) hidden under snow on an 80, east of Grand Rapids
new.pl: An 80-acre slash tract about 12 mi east of Grand Rapids along the Duluth road (US 2, between Philbin and Warba) and 2 mi north of it, Itasca County; tract not yet placed
new.st: After three men robbed a Camden Park State Bank messenger on a Minneapolis streetcar (27 Oct 1933), they were said to have hidden about $9,000 cash on an 80-acre farm east of Grand Rapids. Two Jan 1934 papers: an old farmer-trapper saw two of the robbers drive to the edge of an 80 he owned, go into the slash near dark and come out 1.5 hours later with an ax and a package; heavy snow fell that night. In Jan 1934 the sheriff guarded the spot, crowds dug the snowbanks, and the insurer offered a reward. Coverage stops about 11 Jan 1934 with the money still hidden; two of the men were convicted. About 12 mi E of Grand Rapids, 2 mi N of the Duluth road (US 2). No recovery reported in 1934.
new.t: A quiet find after the snow melted is possible and Itasca papers are not online, so the 1934 Grand Rapids Herald-Review is the check before any trip. Private: permission.
src: Minneapolis Star, 3 Jan 1934, p. 9; 4 Jan 1934, p. 1; 9 Jan 1934, p. 2
Minneapolis Star Tribune, 12 Jan 1934, p. 9; 16 Jan 1934, p. 7
pinev: From the Jan 1934 report: about 12 road miles east of Grand Rapids on US 2 (between Philbin and Warba) and 2 mi north; 3 km covers the 12-16 mile spread between reports.
